chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who became forgetful behind an Imam after he had begun the salat (prayer), so he said nothing, did not say the takbir, did not utter tasbih, and did not recite the tashahhud until he gave salam. He said: His salat (prayer) is valid, and there are no two sajdahs of forgetfulness upon him when he forgets behind the Imam, because the Imam is guarantor for the salat (prayer) of those behind him.
So the proper way of understanding this report is one of two possibilities; one of them is that he guarantees only the recitation and nothing else, which indicates that.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: bearing responsibility or guarantee in the context of congregational prayer
key_terms.يُكَبِّرْ: to pronounce the takbir in prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets dhikr and tashahhud while praying behind the Imam, is his salat valid and must he perform sajdatā al-sahw?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a follower in congregational salat (prayer) who omits several utterances out of forgetfulness while praying behind the Imam. It states that his salat (prayer) remains valid and that sajdatā al-sahw are not required, while the closing note indicates a juristic effort to understand the report in light of the Imam's responsibility for the prayer of those following him.
